title: Hybrid autoscaler for embedding inference combining predictive and reactive modes
creator: Asha Patel
description: Design and implement a hybrid autoscaling controller for the embeddings inference service that combines short-term predictive forecasting with a fast reactive controller. Goal: reduce p99 tail latency and dropped requests during surges while avoiding excessive reserved capacity and minimizing cost per token.
acceptance_criteria: Autoscaler maintains p99 embedding request latency <= 150ms for 99% of tenants during 2x synthetic burst tests
Queue length smoothing keeps median queue_time_ms within target band and avoids >5% request drops under graduated overload tests
Cost overhead for predictive headroom <= 12% over baseline while reducing throttled requests by >= 60%
Canary rollout completed to 10% of tenants with automatic rollback on defined error/latency thresholds
design_decisions: Two-tier controller: (1) Predictive forecasting module that proposes capacity deltas every 60s using Holt-Winters + light ML residual correction; (2) Reactive PID-ish controller for sub-60s adjustments using admission signals
Use tenant-grouped headroom budgets rather than per-tenant hard reservations to improve multiplexing and fairness
Admission control will use leaky-bucket token accounting per-tenant with shared burst_credits and soft_qos priorities for paid tiers
Keep prefix/KV cache affinity intact: scale actions preferentially on pools where KV cache reclaim is least disruptive
Expose knobs for cost-aware scaling: predictive_headroom_pct and max_burst_capacity to allow Ops to tune spend vs latency
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (spike): build forecasting prototype using historical qps + token-length features and evaluate on 90-day workload traces (2 weeks)
Phase 2 (controller): implement reactive admission controller and smoothing queue; integrate with existing provisioner API (3 weeks)
Phase 3 (integration): add headroom budgeting, tenant-group policies, and burst credit accounting (2 weeks)
Phase 4 (canary): deploy to staging and 10% production tenants, exercise synthetic burst harnesses, iterate on thresholds (2 weeks)
Phase 5 (rollout): 50% -> 100% with monitored ramp and rollback automation (2 weeks)
testing_plan: Replay historical traffic into staging clusters with KV cache enabled to measure cold-warm transition behaviour
Run graduated burst tests: 2x, 4x, 8x over baseline for 10m/30m windows and measure p50/p95/p99 latency and queue_time_ms
Fault-injection: simulate delayed provisioning (slow pod launches) and verify fallback policies and graceful degradation
Chaos: kill prewarmed pools to observe admission controller backpressure and drop patterns
E2E canary checks: dashboard health, error rate, dropped_request_rate, and cost delta telemetry
monitoring_and_dashboard_queries: autoscaler.proposed_delta and autoscaler.applied_delta - for drift analysis
rollout_strategy: Start in staging with real traffic replay; evaluate for 1 week
Canary to 10% traffic with monitoring windows and automated rollback (3 alerts tripped => rollback)
Gradual ramp: 10% -> 30% -> 60% -> 100% over multiple days with manual checkpoints
Provide a kill-switch in Console to disable hybrid autoscaler per-cluster if required
risks_and_mitigations: Forecast over-provisioning increases monthly spend: mitigate by capping predictive_headroom_pct and introducing decay when forecast confidence low
Reactive controller oscillation under noisy signals: mitigate by smoothing windows and hysteresis, add damping factor
KV cache churn when scaling horizontally: bias scale-up to pools with cold-cache-impact < threshold and prefer vertical scaling where available
Tenant unfairness during extreme bursts: implement tenant share accounting and emergency weight-based throttles
Complexity in observability: add detailed autoscaler.delta traces and attach to request traces for per-request root cause
notes: This work is informed by the Jan incident where embedding service saw 3x traffic burst leading to 18% request drops and p99 spikes to 520ms (see incident-2026-01-12)
We prioritize SLO stability for top 100 paying tenants; lower-tier tenants may experience soft throttles during severe overload
Cost modeling show moderate increase in reserved GPU minutes but net savings by avoiding emergency overprovisioning and customer support SLAs
